The Horner buildup interpretation assumes an initially uniform, infinite-acting reservoir with negligible fluid removal during the production period prior to closure. [KB1] [KB3]

In a developed reservoir, production-driven pressure gradients and crossflow between layers can distort the Horner buildup interpretation, even when a single-well model is tempting to use. [KB3] [FIG2]

The Horner method is only valid if the system is initially at constant, uniform pressure and is infinite acting, which is typically the case for appraisal wells in unproduced reservoirs. [KB3]

In a developed reservoir, the presence of no-flow boundaries or interlayer crossflow can significantly affect the pressure response, making the Horner buildup interpretation unreliable. [KB3] [FIG2]

The MBH correction is necessary to adjust the extrapolation of the straight line to the reservoir pressure, which requires knowledge of no-flow boundaries in the vicinity of the well. [KB2] [KB3]
